applied_items.content:
Doctor findings and fixes. `chough doctor` (REQ-cli-055) SHALL find this debt without a native read, and its fixes SHALL use Chough's own steps:
- `unmigrated`: a 0.5.x record (REQ-records-010). The fix SHALL name `chough migrate` and SHALL NOT migrate.
- `leak`: a committed record that matches REQ-records-006, with its file, line and kind and never the text. The fix SHALL name `chough doctor --fix --redact`, which SHALL redact the matches in place and is not a decision, except a match in an ID, a front matter line that gives a record's `id`, its aliases or an ID it references (REQ-records-003): `--redact` SHALL never rewrite an ID, since a redacted ID no longer reads. That finding SHALL name the recovery instead, `chough session shelve <id>` for a session record and a reviewed hand edit for any other record, and SHALL stay `skipped` under `--fix --redact`, while the other matches of the same record are redacted.
- `stale_pointer`: the active pointer names a session that is missing or archived. The fix SHALL remove the pointer.
- `finished_session`: an open session that is finished (REQ-history-006) and has no open awaiting-human gate. The fix SHALL archive it. A session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL instead be `skipped`, naming `chough inbox fold`.
- `unfinished_archive`: a session folder whose story exists and that still holds files. The fix SHALL remove every file in the folder whose bytes are committed at HEAD (REQ-records-012), except two kinds it SHALL keep, so no work is lost (#381): an evidence entry, with the screenshot beside it, that the story does not hold, which is one unless one of the story's receipts has the entry's ID and the receipt the entry gives now (REQ-history-006), so an entry that differs from its receipt is kept too; and an unfolded inbox entry under `agent/inbox/`. A merge that keeps main's archive of a session to which a branch added evidence or an inbox entry leaves such an entry. The finding SHALL then be `skipped`, naming each kept entry, that the story does not hold it, and the way out by hand: keep an evidence entry by moving it with `git mv`, with the screenshot beside it, into an open session's `evidence/` folder and committing that, or drop it with `git rm` in a reviewed commit; for an unfolded inbox entry, add its text again in an open session with `chough inbox add`, then drop the kept copy with `git rm` in a reviewed commit; then run `chough doctor --fix` again. macOS metadata in the folder (REQ-cli-068), committed or not, SHALL be removed with it and never block the fix (#377). Any other file it keeps SHALL be reported as `skipped`, naming the commit to make.
- `stale_gates`: an open session whose native change is archived on HEAD and that has open awaiting-human gates. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL withdraw those gates as `chough checkpoint --clear-awaiting-human` does, recording no human decision, SHALL write that reason, in the person's words and checked as REQ-records-006 checks any written value, as the `withdrawn` field of each withdrawn gate's `gate-closed` entry, so the archived story says why each gate was withdrawn, and SHALL then archive the session as the `finished_session` fix does. A decision fix that was applied SHALL echo the reason it wrote in its finding as `decision_reason`.
- `unfinished_session`: an open, unfinished session named with `--close <id>`. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL close the session as `chough session close <id> --reason` does.
- `timeline_rewritten`: a session or story whose Timeline at HEAD is not an exact prefix of its working Timeline (REQ-history-002). It has no fix; the finding names the entries that differ. An entry SHALL NOT count as rewritten when it equals what redaction makes of HEAD's entry, checked by redacting HEAD's text again as `chough doctor --fix --redact` does, since restoring it would restore the leak; committing the redaction is the way on (#374). Any other difference, a hand edit that writes `<redacted:<kind>>` over ordinary words included, still counts.
- `stale_bug_links`: a bug whose body links an open session's evidence entry that left with its archived session, while that session's story holds it as a receipt. The finding names each such entry and the story. The fix, which is not a decision, SHALL append one Log entry to the bug that links each entry to the archived story (REQ-cli-012) and SHALL change no earlier line; a bug whose body already links the story for an entry is not found for it.
- `alias_conflict`: an ID that is the `id` or alias of two records (REQ-records-003). It has no fix; the finding names both records.
- `oversize`: a committed record, evidence entry or screenshot over its bound (REQ-records-001, REQ-records-005, REQ-records-013). It has no fix; the finding names the file, its size and the bound, and the verify lane's `leaks` step fails on it as it does on `leak`, so CI refuses an oversized receipt.
- `unreadable`: a committed Chough record under `.chough/` that its reader refuses, such as front matter outside the subset of REQ-records-001, which makes `chough status` and `chough next` refuse the project. It has no fix; the finding names the file and the reader's reason with its line, and names `chough session shelve <id>` for an open session's `session.md`, except that a record whose front matter holds a Git conflict marker SHALL name resolving the conflict instead, as its `conflict_markers` finding does (REQ-records-001, #374). A record over its bound is `oversize` instead.
- `records_in_verification`: `.specsync/sdd.json` exists and its `verification_ignored_paths` lacks one of Chough's record folders (REQ-records-014). It has no fix, because Chough never writes SpecSync's policy; the finding names the entries to add.
- `merge_drivers`: in a Git work tree, a clone whose Git config has no command for `merge.chough-bug.driver` or `merge.chough-generated.driver` (a fresh clone has neither), or whose `.gitattributes` lacks one of the merge lines of REQ-cli-047. It is one finding, naming the missing drivers and lines. The fix SHALL set the missing drivers in the clone's local Git config and SHALL NOT write `.gitattributes`, a committed file a person reviews. A missing line SHALL leave the finding `skipped`, naming the lines to add and `chough init`, which appends exactly those.
- `merge_driver_outdated`: the merge drivers are set, and the `chough` they run, found through `PATH` as Git finds it, is missing or reports a version older than the running Chough, so a merge would run older code on these records. It has no fix; the finding names both versions and the install command from the README's toolchain section.

The fixes SHALL run in that order. They SHALL never replace a file, and SHALL leave the bytes of every session and story they do not fix unchanged. Trace: DRIVE-17, DRIVE-16, DRIVE-13, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-4, LIFE-26, LIFE-20.

Acceptance Criteria
- A finished session at stage intent and one at done are archived, a stale pointer is removed, and open work stays open.
- An unmigrated tree reports `unmigrated` naming `chough migrate`, and `--fix` changes nothing under `.chough/`.
- A committed home path reports `leak` without the path; `--fix --redact` replaces it with `<redacted:home-path>` and the next run finds nothing.
- A finished session folder holding an uncommitted file is `unfinished_archive`; `--fix` keeps that file, and after a commit removes the folder.
- A hand-edited earlier timeline entry reports `timeline_rewritten`, and an alias held by two bugs reports `alias_conflict`, each with no fix applied.
- Without `--reason`, a stale gate and a session named by `--close` are skipped with their files unchanged; with `--reason` the gate is withdrawn with no human decision recorded and the session is archived, and the named session is closed with the reason.
- A committed evidence entry whose front matter holds a bare `- -c` block item reports `unreadable` naming the file and the line, and `--fix` leaves it byte-identical and the finding `skipped`.
- A clone with neither merge driver set reports one `merge_drivers` finding naming `chough doctor --fix`, and `--fix` sets both. A `.gitattributes` missing a merge line is reported naming that line, and `--fix` leaves `.gitattributes` byte-identical and the finding `skipped`.
- With both merge drivers set and a `chough` first on `PATH` that reports an older version, `chough doctor` reports one `merge_driver_outdated` finding naming both versions and exits 1; with the same version, or with no driver set, it reports none.
- A committed session record whose `cases` reference holds a token, and whose Goal holds an email, gives a `leak` finding for each line; the one for the ID names `chough session shelve <id>`. `--fix --redact` redacts the email, leaves the ID line byte-identical with its finding `skipped`, and the session still reads.
- After a merge that kept main's archive of a session to which a branch added an evidence entry and an inbox entry, `--fix` removes the folder's other committed files and keeps both entries; the finding is `skipped`, naming each and the way out by hand; the kept files are byte-identical, and after the way out the evidence entry resolves again (#381).
- An evidence entry whose ID a receipt holds but whose receipt it no longer matches is kept as well (#381).
- A `.DS_Store` or `._session.md` in an archived session's folder does not block `--fix`, which removes the folder (#377).
- After `--fix --redact` redacts a leak in a committed Timeline entry, the next run reports no `timeline_rewritten`; a hand edit that writes `<redacted:token>` over ordinary words of an entry is still reported (#374).
- A committed session whose front matter holds a conflict reports `conflict_markers` naming each marker and its line, and its `unreadable` finding names resolving the conflict rather than `chough session shelve` (#374).

Focused next action. `chough next` SHALL print a compact action view, separate from the full `chough status` report: the objective; the current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers; the recorded native change with its read state, summary state, approval and correction validity, terminal evidence validity, native next action and approved-delta result; the next valid action with its reason and, when one applies, its command; the gate for the next main stage; awaiting-human gates; blockers; the checkpoint's open questions; open acceptance-blocking bug IDs that stop this session, with the count of other open bugs, and the ids of open blocking bugs that do not block this session; only the referenced observations that need attention, each once: those that are not current, leaving out a superseded run, an earlier run of a case whose later run the checkpoint also references, with counts for the rest, superseded runs counted apart; the most recent checkpoint decisions, at most 5 with their total, showing the kind and reason of entries that follow the `decided:`, `rejected:` or `failed:` prefix convention and other entries whole; the latest failed observation by its recorded observation time, with the status of each bug that links it; and a pointer to each module's native lesson source with the count and bounded paths of archived SpecSync lesson bundles, without reading lesson text or tracking which bundles were folded; the bundles named SHALL be the newest 3 by recorded finalization timestamp, then directory, with an unreadable timestamp sorting oldest, the same 3 that `knowledge/index.md` links (REQ-cli-043). `chough status` SHALL report the same open questions, all of them, in its checkpoint section. It SHALL print text by default and the same fields as JSON with `--json`, and each form SHALL be at most 16384 bytes, with every list bounded, its total stated and any truncation marked. The same records SHALL give byte-identical output; ordering SHALL use recorded fields and names, never file modification times. At plan, while the native change waits for its definition approval, the next valid action SHALL name the human scope gate, opened with `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>" --drives approve` when none is open and closed with `chough checkpoint --close-gate` and the human's decision, and neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`, so no agent is routed to approve its own scope; an approval on authority the human gave in advance stays as REQ-cli-029 describes. Likewise at accept, neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action for the review, `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <name>`, in any field, the native summary and the gate to done included, so no agent is routed to review its own work; where they show SpecSync's next action there, it SHALL read as the human's review at the review gate. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL derive the next valid action from the same rules and SHALL each make at most one native status read. The move into done archives the session (REQ-history-006), after which `chough next` says there is no open session and names `chough session new <key>`, exiting 0, since that is the normal state after done. While an archived session's folder still holds files (`unfinished_archive`, REQ-history-012), `chough next` SHALL first name finishing the archive: committing the session folder, the story and the journal post when they are not committed, then `chough doctor --fix` (#371). A session stays open at done only while an authorized release is still ahead or unfolded inbox entries keep it open; then, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action SHALL name, release first, `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, since the session archives itself only at the move from release into done; otherwise, while inbox entries are unfolded, including after that move, it SHALL name `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`. It SHALL do so rather than repeat the checkpoint's next action, and SHALL NOT recommend a stage reset. A stage reset SHALL replace the checkpoint's next action. Record files. Every record Chough writes, a session, an archived session story, an evidence entry, a bug, an inbox entry, a journal post and a migration receipt, SHALL be one UTF-8 Markdown file that starts with YAML front matter between two `---` lines, and that file SHALL be the record's only source of truth: no JSON or other twin SHALL be written beside it, and no index, cache or generated note SHALL be read in its place. The front matter SHALL carry the IDs and fields agents parse; the body SHALL carry the record for a human reader. Front matter SHALL use a strict subset of YAML that Chough reads and writes without a new dependency: `key: value` scalars, plain or double-quoted with `\"`, `\\` and `\n` escapes; flow lists `[a, b]`; block lists of scalars; and block lists of flat maps of scalars. Chough SHALL refuse front matter outside that subset, a duplicate key or a missing closing `---`, naming the file, the line and the rule, and SHALL write nothing in that command. A record's body SHALL NOT hold a Git conflict marker: a line that starts with `<<<<<<<` or `>>>>>>>`, or a line of `=======` between such lines (a `=======` line outside them, as a Markdown heading underline, is not one); a line inside a closed fenced code block, as CommonMark reads one, quoting an example or tool output, is not one, but a fence that never closes hides nothing after it, and no fence hides a conflict in a section Chough writes itself, a session's `## Timeline` or an archived story's `## Receipts` (#339). A real conflict Git leaves inside such a fence cannot be told from a quoted one, so no write SHALL be refused for it, and `chough doctor` SHALL only warn of each marker line there (REQ-cli-055). A lone `=======` outside a conflict may be left by a half-resolved conflict, but a heading underline may be followed directly by text, so no write SHALL be refused for it, and `chough doctor` SHALL only warn of it (REQ-cli-055). Chough SHALL refuse a write whose body would hold one as `refused:conflict-markers`, naming the file, the line and the marker, with every file unchanged, and `chough doctor` SHALL report each committed record whose front matter or body holds one as a `conflict_markers` finding naming the file, the line and the marker, which has no fix (#374). Reading SHALL be tolerant: an unknown front matter key SHALL be kept byte for byte, in place, when Chough rewrites the front matter, and SHALL be ignored otherwise; a missing optional key SHALL take its documented default; CRLF line endings SHALL be read as LF. Chough SHALL own only the front matter and the sections it appends to, and SHALL keep every other body byte a person or agent wrote: a write SHALL replace the front matter, append list items to the end of a named section, or create a missing named section at the end of the body, and SHALL do nothing else to an existing body. Files SHALL be written with LF line endings by an atomic replace under the writer lock of REQ-cli-040, or by create-new for a new record. A record SHALL be at most 65,536 bytes, except a session record, an archived session story and a migration receipt, which SHALL be at most 1,048,576, 1,048,576 and 4,194,304 bytes; a record over its bound SHALL be refused with the bound named and every file byte-identical. When a 0.5.x record would migrate into a record that holds a marker, the preview SHALL say that the apply refuses and SHALL NOT offer the apply command, and `chough migrate --apply` SHALL refuse with nothing written, each naming the 0.5.x file to resolve, the record it would become, the line and the marker. Trace: DRIVE-25, DRIVE-26, DRIVE-28, KNOW-32, LIFE-3.

Acceptance Criteria
- Every record kind written by a fixture cycle (session, archived story, evidence, bug, inbox entry, journal post, migration receipt) starts with front matter that the reader parses, and no `.json` file is written under `.chough/` except the local caches of REQ-history-007 and `.chough/preferences.json`.
- A person's edit to a session's Goal paragraph, to a bug's Steps and to an evidence entry's body survives a following stage move, decision, evidence add and bug update byte for byte.
- An unknown front matter key added by hand is kept byte for byte after Chough rewrites that front matter, and a missing optional key reads as its default.
- Front matter with a nested map, an anchor, a duplicate key or no closing line is refused with the file, line and rule named, and nothing is written.
- A CRLF copy of a record reads the same as the LF original.
- A record one byte over its bound is refused naming the bound, with every file unchanged.
- A record write whose body holds a `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` conflict line is refused as `refused:conflict-markers` naming the file, the line and the marker, with every file unchanged; a body with a `=======` heading underline and no conflict is written.

- A conflict after a code fence that never closes, or after a backtick line whose tag holds a backtick, is a marker and the write is refused.

It SHALL print text by default and the same fields as JSON with `--json`, and each form SHALL be at most 16384 bytes, with every list bounded, its total stated and any truncation marked. The same records SHALL give byte-identical output; ordering SHALL use recorded fields and names, never file modification times. At plan, while the native change waits for its definition approval, the next valid action SHALL name the human scope gate, opened with `chough checkpoint --awaiting-human "<gate>" --drives approve` when none is open and closed with `chough checkpoint --close-gate` and the human's decision, and neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <name>`, so no agent is routed to approve its own scope; an approval on authority the human gave in advance stays as REQ-cli-029 describes. Likewise at accept, neither form SHALL pass on SpecSync's own next action for the review, `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <name>`, in any field, the native summary and the gate to done included, so no agent is routed to review its own work; where they show SpecSync's next action there, it SHALL read as the human's review at the review gate. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL derive the next valid action from the same rules and SHALL each make at most one native status read. The move into done archives the session (REQ-history-006), after which `chough next` says there is no open session and names `chough session new <key>`, exiting 0, since that is the normal state after done. While an archived session's folder still holds files (`unfinished_archive`, REQ-history-012), `chough next` SHALL first name finishing the archive: committing the session folder, the story and the journal post when they are not committed, then `chough doctor --fix` (#371). A session stays open at done only while an authorized release is still ahead or unfolded inbox entries keep it open; then, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action SHALL name, release first, `chough stage enter release --reason "<request>"` while an authorized release is still ahead, even with inbox entries unfolded, since the session archives itself only at the move from release into done; otherwise, while inbox entries are unfolded, including after that move, it SHALL name `chough inbox fold`, then `chough doctor --fix`. It SHALL do so rather than repeat the checkpoint's next action, and SHALL NOT recommend a stage reset. A stage reset SHALL replace the checkpoint's next action. In an earlier main stage, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence and no pause, human gate or blocking bug applies, the next valid action SHALL NOT continue the stage; it SHALL say the change is archived and recommend the new cycle, a stage reset that carries a reason followed by a new native change, except at accept, where it SHALL recommend recording done first, with `chough stage advance`, which archives the session. Record files. Every record Chough writes, a session, an archived session story, an evidence entry, a bug, an inbox entry, a journal post and a migration receipt, SHALL be one UTF-8 Markdown file that starts with YAML front matter between two `---` lines, and that file SHALL be the record's only source of truth: no JSON or other twin SHALL be written beside it, and no index, cache or generated note SHALL be read in its place. The front matter SHALL carry the IDs and fields agents parse; the body SHALL carry the record for a human reader. Front matter SHALL use a strict subset of YAML that Chough reads and writes without a new dependency: `key: value` scalars, plain or double-quoted with `\"`, `\\` and `\n` escapes; flow lists `[a, b]`; block lists of scalars; and block lists of flat maps of scalars. Chough SHALL refuse front matter outside that subset, a duplicate key or a missing closing `---`, naming the file, the line and the rule, and SHALL write nothing in that command. A record's body SHALL NOT hold a Git conflict marker: a line that starts with `<<<<<<<` or `>>>>>>>`, or a line of `=======` between such lines (a `=======` line outside them, as a Markdown heading underline, is not one); a line inside a closed fenced code block, as CommonMark reads one, quoting an example or tool output, is not one, but a fence that never closes hides nothing after it, and no fence hides a conflict in a section Chough writes itself, a session's `## Timeline` or an archived story's `## Receipts` (#339). A real conflict Git leaves inside such a fence cannot be told from a quoted one, so no write SHALL be refused for it, and `chough doctor` SHALL only warn of each marker line there (REQ-cli-055). A lone `=======` outside a conflict may be left by a half-resolved conflict, but a heading underline may be followed directly by text, so no write SHALL be refused for it, and `chough doctor` SHALL only warn of it (REQ-cli-055). Chough SHALL refuse a write whose body would hold one as `refused:conflict-markers`, naming the file, the line and the marker, with every file unchanged, and `chough doctor` SHALL report each committed record whose front matter or body holds one as a `conflict_markers` finding naming the file, the line and the marker, which has no fix (#374). A marker SHALL be named by its seven characters only, never the rest of its line, which may carry a branch name or a commit subject (#365). Reading SHALL be tolerant: an unknown front matter key SHALL be kept byte for byte, in place, when Chough rewrites the front matter, and SHALL be ignored otherwise; a missing optional key SHALL take its documented default; CRLF line endings SHALL be read as LF. Chough SHALL own only the front matter and the sections it appends to, and SHALL keep every other body byte a person or agent wrote: a write SHALL replace the front matter, append list items to the end of a named section, or create a missing named section at the end of the body, and SHALL do nothing else to an existing body. Files SHALL be written with LF line endings by an atomic replace under the writer lock of REQ-cli-040, or by create-new for a new record. A record SHALL be at most 65,536 bytes, except a session record, an archived session story and a migration receipt, which SHALL be at most 1,048,576, 1,048,576 and 4,194,304 bytes; a record over its bound SHALL be refused with the bound named and every file byte-identical. When a 0.5.x record would migrate into a record that holds a marker, the preview SHALL say that the apply refuses and SHALL NOT offer the apply command, and `chough migrate --apply` SHALL refuse with nothing written, each naming the 0.5.x file to resolve, the record it would become, the line and the marker. Trace: DRIVE-25, DRIVE-26, DRIVE-28, KNOW-32, LIFE-3.

Acceptance Criteria
- Every record kind written by a fixture cycle (session, archived story, evidence, bug, inbox entry, journal post, migration receipt) starts with front matter that the reader parses, and no `.json` file is written under `.chough/` except the local caches of REQ-history-007 and `.chough/preferences.json`.
- A person's edit to a session's Goal paragraph, to a bug's Steps and to an evidence entry's body survives a following stage move, decision, evidence add and bug update byte for byte.
- An unknown front matter key added by hand is kept byte for byte after Chough rewrites that front matter, and a missing optional key reads as its default.
- Front matter with a nested map, an anchor, a duplicate key or no closing line is refused with the file, line and rule named, and nothing is written.
- A CRLF copy of a record reads the same as the LF original.
- A record one byte over its bound is refused naming the bound, with every file unchanged.
- A record write whose body holds a `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` conflict line is refused as `refused:conflict-markers` naming the file, the line and the marker, with every file unchanged; a body with a `=======` heading underline and no conflict is written.
- With a committed record whose body holds a conflict, `chough doctor` reports a `conflict_markers` finding for each marker line naming the file, the line and the marker, exits 1, and reports none for a tracked file that is not a record.
- A conflict quoted inside a fenced code block, with backtick or tilde fences, is not a marker and the record saves; a lone `=======` with text after it is not refused either.
- A conflict after a code fence that never closes, or after a backtick line whose tag holds a backtick, is a marker and the write is refused.
- A conflict inside an archived story's `## Timeline` or fenced `## Receipts` block is a marker, inside a fence or not.
- A Git conflict left inside a code fence of a session's Goal is not refused on the next write.
- A 0.5.x inbox entry whose text holds a conflict makes the migration preview say the apply refuses, without offering the apply command, and the apply refuse, each naming that 0.5.x file first.
- A conflict whose marker lines name a branch or a commit subject holding a token is refused and reported naming only `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` and the line, never the branch or the subject (#365).
- A committed record whose front matter holds a conflict, as two branches that each set `--objective` leave after a merge, gives a `conflict_markers` finding for each of its marker lines (#374).

Files SHALL be written with LF line endings by an atomic replace under the writer lock of REQ-cli-040, or by create-new for a new record. A record SHALL be at most 65,536 bytes, except a session record, an archived session story and a migration receipt, which SHALL be at most 1,048,576, 1,048,576 and 4,194,304 bytes; a record over its bound SHALL be refused with the bound named and every file byte-identical. When a 0.5.x record would migrate into a record that holds a marker, the preview SHALL say that the apply refuses and SHALL NOT offer the apply command, and `chough migrate --apply` SHALL refuse with nothing written, each naming the 0.5.x file to resolve, the record it would become, the line and the marker. Trace: DRIVE-25, DRIVE-26, DRIVE-28, KNOW-32, LIFE-3.

Acceptance Criteria
- Every record kind written by a fixture cycle (session, archived story, evidence, bug, inbox entry, journal post, migration receipt) starts with front matter that the reader parses, and no `.json` file is written under `.chough/` except the local caches of REQ-history-007 and `.chough/preferences.json`.
- A person's edit to a session's Goal paragraph, to a bug's Steps and to an evidence entry's body survives a following stage move, decision, evidence add and bug update byte for byte.
- An unknown front matter key added by hand is kept byte for byte after Chough rewrites that front matter, and a missing optional key reads as its default.
- Front matter with a nested map, an anchor, a duplicate key or no closing line is refused with the file, line and rule named, and nothing is written.
- A CRLF copy of a record reads the same as the LF original.
- A record one byte over its bound is refused naming the bound, with every file unchanged.
- A record write whose body holds a `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` conflict line is refused as `refused:conflict-markers` naming the file, the line and the marker, with every file unchanged; a body with a `=======` heading underline and no conflict is written.
- With a committed record whose body holds a conflict, `chough doctor` reports a `conflict_markers` finding for each marker line naming the file, the line and the marker, exits 1, and reports none for a tracked file that is not a record.
- A conflict quoted inside a fenced code block, with backtick or tilde fences, is not a marker and the record saves; a lone `=======` with text after it is not refused either.
- A conflict after a code fence that never closes, or after a backtick line whose tag holds a backtick, is a marker and the write is refused.
- A conflict inside an archived story's `## Timeline` or fenced `## Receipts` block is a marker, inside a fence or not.
- A Git conflict left inside a code fence of a session's Goal is not refused on the next write.
- A 0.5.x inbox entry whose text holds a conflict makes the migration preview say the apply refuses, without offering the apply command, and the apply refuse, each naming that 0.5.x file first.
- A conflict whose marker lines name a branch or a commit subject holding a token is refused and reported naming only `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` and the line, never the branch or the subject (#365).

Chough's records stay out of SpecSync's verification. The folders Chough writes while work is in progress, `.chough/sessions/`, `.chough/archive/` and `.chough/bugs/`, SHALL hold only Chough's records: no case definition, preference, reading guide or other input that a change's verification needs SHALL be written under them, and `.chough/cases/`, `.chough/preferences.json`, `.chough/README.md` and `knowledge/` SHALL stay outside them. These three prefixes are what a project lists in SpecSync's documented exclusion, `verification_ignored_paths` in `.specsync/sdd.json` (SpecSync 6.1.2 and later), so that a Chough record written after `specsync change check --commit`, whether left untracked or committed, leaves the recorded verification current, in the author's tree and in a reviewer's clean checkout alike; `.chough/local/` is already Git-ignored and never part of it. Chough SHALL read that policy and SHALL never write it: `chough doctor` SHALL report `records_in_verification` (REQ-history-012) while `.specsync/sdd.json` exists and its list lacks any of the three prefixes, naming the missing entries, the SpecSync version that supports them and that adding them is an ordinary reviewed change to `.specsync/sdd.json`; `chough init` SHALL print the same advice; and the migration plan and receipt SHALL list it as a follow-up (REQ-records-009). The spec files read for this advice SHALL be found without following a symbolic link, to a file or to a folder, so a link out of the project cannot make outside code count and a link cycle cannot hang `chough doctor` or `chough init`; the walk SHALL read at most 4,096 entries and 32 folders deep, and when it stops at that bound, the advice SHALL say so, naming the bound, so a root file beyond it is not silently missed (#402). `chough next` SHALL say when Chough writes are safe: with the three entries in force, that Chough's records may be written and committed at any point of the native order; without them, that Chough's records are committed before `change check --commit` and nothing under `.chough/` is written until finalize. While SpecSync covers the whole repository, through `source_dirs` holding `.` in `.specsync/config.toml` or `.` in the policy's `meaningful_paths`, SpecSync refuses those entries as overlapping, so the advice of `chough doctor` and `chough init` SHALL instead name those settings, say why (SpecSync refuses an entry that overlaps them and, for `source_dirs`, counts the skill bundle `chough init` installs as uncovered source), and say to narrow `source_dirs` to the folders that hold the code, for example `["src"]`, and keep `.` out of `meaningful_paths`, then list the missing entries; When a file a spec covers sits at the repository root, so there is no code folder to narrow to (#354), the advice SHALL instead say to add the skill bundle's and Chough's folders (`.chough`, and `.agents` or the host's skill folder) to `exclude_dirs`, which keeps them out of coverage, and that the list needs the code moved into a folder or SpecSync's fix, CorvidLabs/spec-sync#1083. `chough init` SHALL give its advice with no policy too, and Chough SHALL write neither file. When SpecSync refuses the list because an open change's affected paths overlap it, Chough SHALL pass that refusal through and name the change. Trace: DRIVE-4, FLOW-16.

Acceptance Criteria
- With the three entries listed and real SpecSync at the CI pin, an untracked evidence entry present while `change check --commit` runs leaves verification current in that tree and in a clean clone of the pushed commit, whose workspace digest matches the recorded one (spec-sync #1045's case); the same steps without the entries leave the clone's verification stale, as the control.
- With the three entries listed, a `chough checkpoint`, a `chough evidence add` and a `chough bug add` written after `change check --commit`, and then committed, leave `specsync change status` reporting verification current and the audit passing, and the review then records (the #212 case); without the entries the same writes make verification stale, as the control.
- A case definition changed under `.chough/cases/` after `change check --commit` still makes verification stale, so nothing a change's verification needs is hidden.
- With a prefix missing, `chough doctor` reports `records_in_verification` naming the missing entries and writes nothing; with all three listed it reports nothing; `.specsync/sdd.json` is byte-identical after every Chough command.
- `chough next` says Chough's writes are safe at any point with the entries in force, and gives the commit-first order without them.
- With `source_dirs = ["."]` and no policy, `chough init` prints the narrowing advice naming it, the overlap refusal and the skill bundle; with a policy whose `meaningful_paths` also holds `.`, `chough doctor`'s `records_in_verification` names both settings and says to narrow, then list the missing entries; once both are narrowed the advice is the list again; `.specsync/config.toml` and `.specsync/sdd.json` stay byte-identical.
- With `source_dirs = ["."]` and a spec covering a file at the repository root, `chough init` and `chough doctor` advise adding `.chough` and the installed skill folder to `exclude_dirs` and say the list needs the code in a folder or CorvidLabs/spec-sync#1083, never naming a folder to narrow to; once those folders are excluded, only the list's part is left.
- With `specs/` holding a symlink to a spec file outside the project, a folder symlink that points outside the project and two folder symlinks back to the project, `chough doctor` and `chough init` finish and give the advice they give without them; a `specs/` with more entries than the bound gives the advice with a note naming the bound (#402).
